slides.title:
Missed a day?
Your habit is *fine*.
slides.kicker: 4 rules for people who restart every Monday
slides.alt: Cover: Missed a day? Your habit is fine. Four rules for people who restart every Monday.

slides.title: One missed day is noise. *Two* is a pattern.
slides.body: Protect one line: never miss twice in a row.
slides.alt: Rule 1: one missed day is noise, two is a pattern. Never miss twice in a row.

slides.fact:
*66 days* on average.
Missing one didn't matter.
slides.source: Lally et al., European Journal of Social Psychology, 2010 (96 people; range 18 to 254 days)
slides.alt: Myth: a habit takes 21 days. Fact: 66 days on average in a 2010 study, and missing one day didn't matter.

slides.title: Shrink it on bad days
slides.body:
No time for 20 minutes? Do 2.
On a bad day, the rep counts, not the size.
slides.alt: Rule 2: shrink it on bad days. Do two minutes instead of twenty.

slides.title: Count weeks, not days
slides.body: A streak counter calls 6 out of 7 a failure. Your week calls it a good week.
slides.alt: Rule 3: count weeks, not days. Six out of seven is a good week.

slides.title: Tie it to something you already do
slides.body: After coffee. Before email. When the laptop opens. Pick a cue you never skip.
slides.alt: Rule 4: tie the habit to something you already do, like coffee or opening the laptop.

slides.title: The 4 rules
slides.alt: Recap of the four rules: never miss twice, shrink it on bad days, count weeks not days, tie it to a cue.

slides.title: plodd counts your *week*
slides.body: Miss Wednesday. Still a good week.
slides.alt: Screenshot of plodd's week view: 6 of 7 days done, Wednesday missed.
